moneyFound.headline: Money found: about €752 a year after DIRT (€572 car loan: cleared from savings; €180 current account: €16,000 moved to bunq Savings Account).

parts.label: Car loan: cleared from savings
parts.detail: €9,000 of savings against €9,000 at 9%: €673.56 of interest not paid in the next twelve months, less €101.30 the same money would earn after DIRT in bunq Savings Account.

parts.label: Current account: €16,000 moved to bunq Savings Account
parts.detail: €180.10 a year after DIRT in bunq Savings Account, against €0 at 0% now, with access kept.

notCounted.label: Current account: MoCo EasySaver
notCounted.why: €45 a year more at MoCo EasySaver’s rate, but that rate rests on CCPC’s one figure: the provider may pay it only for a period or on part of the balance.

moneyFound.basis: A year’s figures, after DIRT at 33%: idle cash against the best confirmed instant-access rate (only where its current rate was given), debt interest not paid in the next twelve months less what the same money would earn, and a mortgage switch’s lower repayment. Bonuses, cashback and rates resting on CCPC’s one figure are not counted.

findings.headline: €25,000 in Current account earns €0 a year after DIRT
findings.detail: At 0% it earns €0 a year. The highest instant-access rate Saoi holds (MoCo EasySaver) would pay about €352.50 after DIRT on the same money, with access kept.

findings.headline: Car loan at 9% costs more than any savings account earns
findings.detail: €9,000 at 9% costs about €810 a year in interest. The same money in the highest-paying instant-access account would earn about €126.90 after DIRT. Interest still to pay at the current repayment: €1,274.96. €25,000 is held in savings.

findings.headline: Help to Buy: up to €35,000 towards a new build, for a first-time buyer
findings.detail: Revenue refunds the lesser of 10% of a new build’s or self-build’s price (up to €500,000), €35,000, and the Income Tax and DIRT paid over the last four tax years, for homes bought or built by 2029-12-31. With €25,000 saved and €62,000 income, the Central Bank limits allow a price up to €250,000, or €303,333.33 for a new build with Help to Buy towards the deposit. saoi_first_home works it out for a price.

candidateGoals.label: Clearing the highest-rate debt
candidateGoals.why: A debt costs more in interest than any savings account earns.

candidateGoals.label: Idle money earning more
candidateGoals.why: Money is held at a rate well below what instant access pays.

assumptions: Savings rates are compared after DIRT at 33%, over twelve months, in instant-access accounts.
Variable rates are assumed to stay as published.
Goal pace counts savings held and monthly saving before interest; every goal is set against all savings held.
Help to Buy as Revenue states it (https://www.revenue.ie/en/property/help-to-buy-incentive/how-much-can-you-claim.aspx, checked 2026-11-09).
attributions: Source: Competition and Consumer Protection Commission, www.ccpc.ie
next: Nothing is stored from a review. These findings are figures for the customer to weigh; they decide what matters. Once they have chosen goals (with an amount and a date where they have one), saoi_build_plan turns this into a plan with products, figures and the month each goal is reached. Every plan comes with a link that opens it in the Saoi app, held for 24 hours and then deleted unless opened: a card that Saoirse, Saoi’s assistant, knows and can talk through, and signing in keeps it across devices.
